payload.purpose_context: The nightly backup records ten facts about each run, including the weekly integrity verdict from restic check. Six of those ten are written and then ignored by every health surface that exists, so a backup whose repository has been proven corrupt still reports healthy and nobody is told until a restore is attempted and fails. This mission replaces the habit of remembering to read each new field with a contract: every field a backup emits must be declared either as one that decides health, with an explicit definition of good, or as one kept only for diagnosis. A test reads the fields the backup actually emits and fails if any of them is undeclared. The same contract is built once and used by both machines that run backups, so the rule cannot drift apart between them.
payload.purpose_tldr: Make every field a backup writes about its own health actually get read, so a repository proven corrupt can never report healthy.

payload.question: For office2's ledger, how many of the v0.2 adjudication rules are adopted now: only integrity_check_passed (rest diagnostic_only), also the rules office2's already-emitted fields can support (snapshot_count wipe-detection, future-dated timestamp guard), or also add the fields office2 does not yet emit (files_processed, source_roots_present, repo_fs_free_bytes) for full parity?

payload.final_answer: adopt-rules-on-existing-fields: declare all 10 emitted keys; adjudicate integrity_check_passed (true|null good, false unhealthy), snapshot_count (>1 on an established repo, catching a wiped-and-reinitialised repo), and add a future-dating guard to the existing snapshot_timestamp_utc freshness rule; restic_exit_code {0,3} and prune_exit_code {0} keep their current good-sets. schema_version, snapshot_id, repo_size_bytes, script_finished_at_utc and integrity_check_run are declared diagnostic_only. NO change to scripts/office2/restic-backup.sh - every rule reads a field the producer already emits, so no Tier-2 producer deploy. Adding files_processed / source_roots_present / repo_fs_free_bytes to office2 is explicitly out of scope for this mission.

payload.question: Which producers must have a declared key ledger enforced by the test in THIS mission: only the backup pointers (office2 restic now, office4 restic via #913), or all 17 pointer-emitting components in the service inventory?

payload.final_answer: backup-pointers-only-mechanism-generic: the contract and its enforcing test helper are built GENERICALLY so any pointer-emitting component can adopt them by declaring a ledger, but enforcement in this mission covers only the restic backup pointers - office2's now, office4's when #913 builds its producer. The other 16 pointer-emitting components in service-inventory.json get a documented adoption path plus a follow-up issue; they are explicitly out of scope here because 16 of them have no deterministic execution harness and several emit from OpenClaw agent steps, so enforcing them would mean building harnesses as the bulk of the work and would degrade the test into asserting a hand-maintained key list - the very defect the contract replaces.

payload.question: Where does the per-producer key ledger live: as machine-readable data inside service-inventory.json's health_check block (converting the existing 'expected' prose to data), as a dedicated pointer-ledgers.json under architecture/data covering both hosts, or as a Python declaration module in scripts/canary/?

payload.final_answer: inventory-health-check-block: the key ledger is declared as machine-readable data inside each component's existing health_check block in docs/design/architecture/data/service-inventory.json, with adjudicated keys carrying explicit good-sets and a diagnostic_only list. The adjudication rules currently written as English prose in health_check.expected become data. probes.py stays convention-generic and reads the declared ledger rather than gaining any component-keyed table, preserving its stated 'do NOT special-case component names' invariant and following the precedent set by success_status_values in #891. The existing blocking architecture-data CI validator is extended to cover the new structure. Consequence to carry into #913: office4's ledger becomes a component entry carrying host: office4, and the inventory has zero office4 entries today, so that placement is confirmed by #913 and is not decided here.

Codex confirmed the substance: it hand-built the #902/FR-009 regression against the shipped code with restic-backup's REAL ledger loaded, and null / 'not-a-date' / numeric anchors ALL read unhealthy with no fall-through to another TIMESTAMP_KEYS candidate. Anchor binding, non-anchor bounds, the strict 300s skew boundary, naive-timestamp handling, malformed-ledger totality and outcome mapping all correct. Ledger-free path produced identical verdicts AND identical evidence vs the parent implementation. 264 canary tests pass. Scope clean.

It rejected on PROCESS only: T019's refactor and the ledger wiring landed in one commit (2e0105f0), so the no-op proof existed only in the implementer's report rather than in inspectable history.

Two reasons for the override. First, my WP04 prompt required the refactor to be done FIRST and proven a no-op; it never required a separate commit, so this is an unstated requirement. Second and decisive: I produced the missing evidence directly and more strongly. I extracted _explicit_error from 2e0105f0^ (parent) and from the shipped tree and ran a differential test over 2520 generated pointer shapes - exit codes incl. None/str/bool/float, timestamps incl. null/unparseable/numeric/dict/offset forms, prune codes, and the errors/error/status/exit_status/cycle_error conventions, plus pointers carrying NO restic_exit_code at all. Result: 0 mismatches. The refactor is provably behaviour-preserving, which is the ONLY thing the commit ordering was instrumental in establishing. A separate commit would merely have shown the suite green at that point; this shows the two implementations are functionally indistinguishable.

Also noted: the implementer independently proved its own T023 regression tests can FAIL, by temporarily patching in the naive-wrong integration (fall through to TIMESTAMP_KEYS instead of the anchor) and confirming 3 real_ledger tests went red on exactly the null/unparseable/numeric timestamp cases. A regression test nobody has watched fail is unverified; this one was verified.
